title: The Growing 25
lede: Twenty-five Series B to D companies scaling fast. Mostly US, picked for fresh money, strong backers and real traction.
method: Every company here is already on the Well Run board. We keep the ones whose headquarters and most of the team are in the US, that are still private and independent, and whose latest round is Series B, C or D. Then we rank by promise: how recent and how strong the last round was, who led it, real traction (revenue, customers, usage) and hiring momentum. Each pick gets a fresh check for layoffs, lawsuits and down rounds; anything unresolved stays off. We leave out companies already valued above about $5 billion; they have grown, not growing. Hand-picked, updated as rounds land. Each line links to its source.

picks.name: Traversal
picks.why: Hit a $1B valuation 17 months out of stealth; ARR grew 9x this year as Pepsi, Amex and Nubank put its AI SRE on production.

picks.name: Applied Compute
picks.why: Helps companies train and run their own AI; zero to a $100M run rate in under 18 months, valuation up 2.5x since April.

picks.name: Rox
picks.why: AI revenue agents for the Global 2000; ARR up 10x in its first year in market, now valued at $1.3B.

picks.name: Forus
picks.why: AI that gets patients onto prescribed medicines; valuation tripled to $3B in four months, used for patients in 85% of US ZIP codes.

picks.name: Arena
picks.why: The AI leaderboard turned business: run-rate went from $30M in January to $100M+ by June, and its valuation nearly doubled to $3.1B.

picks.name: Serval
picks.why: AI that automates IT and HR requests to take on ServiceNow; third round in 12 months, team up 10x, two Fortune 20 customers added.

picks.name: Wispr Flow
picks.why: Voice dictation people actually switched to: revenue up 30x year over year, valuation nearly tripled to $2B in nine months.

picks.name: Tutor Intelligence
picks.why: Rents factory and warehouse robots by the hour, guided by remote human tutors; working in nearly 4x as many facilities as a year ago.

picks.name: Blacksmith
picks.why: Runs code builds and tests for 10,000+ companies; ARR up 17x since January as AI-written code floods the pipeline.

picks.name: Valon
picks.why: Operating system for mortgage servicing; signed $200M+ in contracted ARR within six months of selling it, now under contract for 1 in 6 US mortgages.

picks.name: Charta Health
picks.why: AI chart review for medical billing; revenue up 10x in 12 months, third round in under two years.

picks.name: Profound
picks.why: Helps brands show up in AI answers; 1,000+ enterprise brands including a third of the Fortune 100, raised again seven months after its C.

picks.name: Rillet
picks.why: AI-native ERP winning deals off NetSuite and Oracle; 600+ customers and ARR doubled in three months, third raise in a year.

picks.name: Pace
picks.why: AI agents for insurance back offices at Prudential and WTW; ARR up 15x+ through the first three quarters of 2026.

picks.name: Thatch
picks.why: Lets employers give workers a health budget instead of one group plan; revenue up nearly 7x in a year, 5,000+ employers.

picks.name: Candid Health
picks.why: Autonomous medical billing for 200+ providers; ARR up 190% year over year, valuation tripled since 2025.

picks.name: Parallel Web Systems
picks.why: Web search built for AI agents; 100,000+ developers and a $2B valuation five months after its A.

picks.name: Basis
picks.why: AI agents that do accounting firm work; now in roughly 40% of the top 25 US firms, team up 2.5x in a year.

picks.name: Omni
picks.why: AI analytics from the Looker founders; ARR up 4x last year, tripled again in early 2026, and now profitable.

picks.name: Monaco
picks.why: AI-native sales platform from Sam Blond; went from zero revenue in February to adding seven figures of ARR a month.

picks.name: Broccoli AI
picks.why: AI front desk for home-services businesses; $15M+ ARR in under two years across 1,500+ businesses.

picks.name: Albert Invent
picks.why: Chemistry-native AI for R&D at BASF, Henkel and Kenvue; scientists on the platform up 6x in a year.

picks.name: Confido
picks.why: Back office for consumer brands; 250+ brands including Mars and Unilever divisions, 5x growth since its A.

picks.name: General Medicine
picks.why: The PillPack founders' healthcare store; 2,900+ priced services and a16z bio's largest check to date.

picks.name: Stuut
picks.why: AI agents for accounts receivable; raised its B ten months after its A, with most collections now running hands-free.
